focus: 'used to' /juːstə/ reduction · 'would' → 'd for repeated past · 'didn't use to' · weak 'to' in habits · past-habit rhythm
focus_ar: 'used to' /juːstə/، و 'would' → 'd للماضي المتكرر، و 'didn't use to'، و 'to' الخفيفة، وإيقاع العادات الماضية
arabic_challenge: 'Used to' is pronounced /juːstə/ (one blended unit, /s/ not /z/), which learners often say as 'used-too' with a full /tuː/. 'Would' for past habits reduces to 'd, and both need weak 'to'.

isolation.instructions: 'Used to' blends into /juːstə/: the 'd' + 't' merge into a single /s...t/, and 'to' weakens. 'I used to play' = /aɪ juːstə pleɪ/. Not 'used-too'.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'used to' بتندمج في /juːstə/: الـ d+t بيبقوا /s..t/ و 'to' تخف. 'I used to play' = /juːstə/.

sentence_practice: We used to live in Cairo.
She used to be very shy.
daily_drills.record_this: When I was young, I used to play football every day. We used to live in Cairo, near the river. My sister used to be very shy, but now she's confident.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'used to play'. Is it a blended /juːstə/ with an /s/, not 'used-too'?

isolation.instructions: For repeated past ACTIONS, 'would' works like 'used to' and reduces to 'd: 'Every summer we'd visit grandma'. (Use it for actions, not states.) Stress the main verb.
isolation.instructions_ar: للأفعال المتكررة في الماضي، 'would' زي 'used to' وتخف لـ 'd: 'we'd visit'. (للأفعال مش الحالات.)

sentence_practice: Every summer we'd visit my grandmother.
On Fridays we'd go to the market.
daily_drills.record_this: Every summer we'd visit my grandmother in the village. In the evenings she'd always tell us old stories. And on Fridays we'd all go to the market together.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'we'd visit'. Is 'would' contracted to 'd, with stress on 'visit'?

isolation.instructions: Negative and question drop the 'd': 'didn't USE to' /juːs tə/ and 'Did you USE to…?'. Note it's 'use to' (no 'd') after 'did'. Say 'didn't yoos-tə'.
isolation.instructions_ar: النفي والسؤال بيشيلوا الـ 'd': 'didn't use to' و 'Did you use to…?'. بعد 'did' تبقى 'use to' بدون d.

pair: I didn't use to like it

sentence_practice: I didn't use to like coffee.
Did you use to live here?
She didn't use to work weekends.
daily_drills.record_this: I didn't use to like coffee, but now I drink it every day. Did you use to live here as a child? My mother didn't use to work weekends, but things changed.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'didn't use to like'. Is it 'use to' (no 'd') after 'didn't'?

isolation.instructions: Do not confuse: 'I used to smoke' /juːstə/ (past habit, now stopped) vs 'I'm used to the noise' /juːst tuː/ (accustomed, + noun/-ing). Different meaning, slightly different stress.
isolation.instructions_ar: متخلطش: 'I used to smoke' (عادة ماضية) مقابل 'I'm used to the noise' (معتاد على، + اسم/-ing).

pair: are you used to the work?

sentence_practice: I used to live in a village.
Now I'm used to living in the city.
I'm not used to the noise yet.
daily_drills.record_this: I used to live in a small village, so at first the city was strange. But now I'm used to living here, and I've got used to the traffic. I'm still not used to the noise at night, though.
daily_drills.self_check: Can you tell your two 'used to' apart — past habit (+ base verb) vs accustomed (+ noun/-ing)?

isolation.instructions: These stories contrast past and present: 'I USED to be shy, but NOW I'm confident'. Stress 'used to' lightly and put the weight on the contrast words (shy / now / confident).
isolation.instructions_ar: القصص دي بتقارن الماضي بالحاضر: 'I used to be shy, but now...'. النبر على كلمات المقارنة.
practice: I used to be SHY, but NOW I'm CONfident
we used to WALK, now we DRIVE

sentence_practice: I used to be shy, but now I'm confident.
We used to walk everywhere; now we drive.
People used to write letters; nowadays they text.
daily_drills.record_this: I used to be really shy, but now I'm much more confident. We used to walk everywhere as kids; these days we just drive. People used to write long letters; nowadays they simply text.
daily_drills.self_check: Does the contrast (used to … but now …) come through, with the change words stressed?

challenge_sentences: I used to play football, and every weekend we'd have a match.
Did you use to live here?
I didn't use to like coffee, but now I love it.
I used to live in a village; now I'm used to the city.
daily_drills.record_this: I used to play football when I was young, and every weekend we'd have a big match. Did you use to live in this area? I didn't use to like coffee, but now I love it. I used to live in a village; now I'm used to the busy city.
daily_drills.self_check: Three checks: blended 'used to' /juːstə/, contracted 'we'd' for habits, and 'use to' (no d) after did/didn't.

test_yourself.instructions: Record yourself comparing your past life with now. Then listen back and check each feature.
test_yourself.instructions_ar: سجّل نفسك وانت تقارن حياتك قديمًا بالآن، وبعدين اسمع وراجع كل نقطة.
test_yourself.passage: Life used to be very different when I was a child. We used to live in a small village, and we didn't use to have much money, but we were happy. Every morning I'd walk to school with my friends, and after class we'd play in the fields until sunset. My grandmother used to cook for the whole family, and on special days she'd make my favourite dish. I didn't use to like vegetables, but she'd always find a way to make me eat them! These days everything has changed. I live in the city now, and I'm used to a faster life. Sometimes I miss how things used to be.

sounds_to_check.'used to' /juːstə/: used to be, used to live, used to cook
sounds_to_check.'would' → 'd (repeated past): I'd walk, we'd play, she'd make, she'd find
sounds_to_check.'didn't use to' (no d): didn't use to have, didn't use to like
sounds_to_check.'be used to' (accustomed): I'm used to a faster life
sounds_to_check.past/present contrast: used to be different … these days everything has changed

scoring_guide.90_100: 'used to' blended, 'would' contracted, negatives correct, contrast clear. Ready for week 9.
scoring_guide.50_69: 'used to' said as 'used-too', or 'didn't used to'. Repeat days 1 and 3.

for_arabic_speakers: 'used to' blends into /juːstə/ (with /s/) — one unit, not 'used-too'.
'would' → 'd expresses repeated past ACTIONS (not states): 'we'd visit'.
After 'did/didn't' it's 'use to' (no 'd'): 'Did you use to…?', 'I didn't use to…'.
Don't confuse past-habit 'used to + verb' with accustomed 'be used to + noun/-ing'.
supplementary_notes.recording_requirement: Record the 'record_this' line daily; compare day 7 with day 1.
